newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp confident of Thyssen takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: Krupp confident of Thyssen takeover bid.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Krupp on Tuesday confirmed it planned to launch a takeover bid for rival Thyssen AG and that it was confident it would succeed.
"Krupp plans to make a takeover bid," a company spokesman told Reuters. "We think it is fairly certain to succeed."

A Krupp spokesman said that the company's chairman Gerhard Cromme earlier told a gathering of angry steelworkers that it would make sense to bring the two companies together into a large steel and engineering group.

The company said it would make an official statement on its takeover plans later in the day. Thyssen AG, which said it would defend itself against the hostile takeover together with an unidentified parnter, plans to hold a news conference at 1400 GMT at its headquarters in Duesseldorf.
The companies met earlier in the day with government officials from the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, which is governed by a coalition of Social Democrats (SPD) and environmentalist Greens.

State premier Johannes Rau had earlier confirmed that Krupp planned to launch a bid for Thyssen amid protests by angry steel workers who called for the mammoth merger to be blocked, fearing the loss of thousands of jobs.
